newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair congratulates Jospin on poll victory.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair congratulates Jospin on poll victory.

text.p: Britain's new Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair congratulated French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin on his stunning election victory in Sunday's parliamentary elections.
Blair conveyed his best wishes to Jospin in a late night telephone call after preliminary results gave France's combined left an absolute majority in the National Assembly.
It was a crushing result for President Jacques Chirac who called the election 10 months early and must now share power with a left-wing government.

A spokeswoman at Blair's office said: "He congratulated Mr Jospin on the result of the French election and he has spoken to President Chirac to say he wishes to confirm his continuing cooperation with the French government, and he, of course, is going to see President Chirac on June 11 in Paris."

Blair, who won his own landslide victory a month ago to oust Britain's Conservatives after 18 years in power, would not be drawn about comparisons between the two elections or Jospin's earlier comments that the victories will "raise a magnificent hope in Europe."
The French results topped British television news and dominated the front pages of the country's newspapers on Monday.
The left-leaning Guardian newspaper hailed Jospin's win and said it opened the way for a unique European alliance with Blair's New Labour.
"This will be the first time since the Fifth Republic was founded in 1958 that left-of-centre governments will coincide in Paris and London," it said.

The Financial Times described the result as a stinging blow for Chirac and a personal triumph for Jospin. But it warned that it would create uncertainty over European ecnomic and monetary union (EMU) and could threaten the privatisaiton of France Telecom and the defence company Thomson-CSF.
"He (Jospin) has made great play of the evils of hard capitalism offered by the political right, and stressed the need for a more human, social approach without further austerity measures," it added.
The Times put it more buntly. "This is an election about jobs," it said, adding that the lurch back to the left showed the volatility of the electorate and the fear of change.

"France could yet join EMU if only to escape a meltdown of the franc. M Jospin's key adviser on Europe is expected to be Jacque DeLors, and all the likely candidates for the Quai d'Orsay are convinced federalists," it said.
"If EMU goes ahead with millions on the dole, the ultimate victor of this election is likely to prove Jean-Marie Le Pen's xenophobic National Front."
